extracted.intended_audience: machine learning researchers, NeurIPS authors and reviewers, and conference organizers interested in reproducibility practices
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and evaluation criteria for improving reproducibility of empirical machine learning research, as implemented in the NeurIPS 2019 program (code policy, community reproducibility challenge, and the ML reproducibility checklist).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproducibility (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Reproducible work consists of re-doing an experiment using the same data and same analytical tools."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus of the paper is on reproducing results with the same data and analytical tools; assume small/modest modifications to analytical tools are negligible for the definition used here.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replicability (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Replicable work considers different data (presumably sampled from similar distribution or method).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish from reproducibility: replication uses different datasets to test whether findings generalize.

rubrics_metrics.name: Robustness (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Robust work assumes the same data but different analysis (such as reimplementation of the code, perhaps different computer architecture).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Robustness emphasizes independent reimplementation and analysis to verify results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generalisability (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Generalisable work leads to the same conclusions despite considering different data and different analytical tools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highest-level notion: different data and tools still support same scientific conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open science / share code and data
rubrics_metrics.description: "Open Science is transparent and accessible knowledge..." and includes "making code, data and scientific communications publicly available."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sharing artifacts (code, data, supplementary materials) improves reproducibility, transparency, and accelerates integration of findings into practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Code submission policy (encourage and expect code by camera-ready)
rubrics_metrics.description: "To foster reproducibility, we highly encourage authors to submit code. Reproducibility of results and easy availability of code will be taken into account in the decision-making process." Also: "We expect (but not require) accompanying code to be submitted with accepted papers that contribute and present experiments with a new algorithm."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Code is encouraged and expected at camera-ready for accepted papers with experiments; it is not mandatory at submission but may be provided then. Availability of code was correlated with higher reviewer scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary material size & content limits
rubrics_metrics.description: "Authors may submit up to 100MB of supplementary material, such as proofs, derivations, data, or source code."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the supplementary material allowance to provide proofs, derivations, datasets (where possible), and source code; adhere to platform limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: A clear description of the mathematical setting, algorithm, and/or model
rubrics_metrics.description: "A clear description of the mathematical setting, algorithm, and/or model."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manuscripts should unambiguously describe the model and mathematical assumptions so others can reproduce or reimplement the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe how experiments were run
rubrics_metrics.description: "For all figures and tables that present empirical results, indicate if you include: A description of how experiments were run."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide procedural details (training protocol, hyperparameters, exact data splits, compute environment, seeds where applicable, preprocessing steps) so results can be re-executed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define measures / statistics used to report results
rubrics_metrics.description: "A clear definition of the specific measure or statistics used to report results."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly define metrics (e.g., accuracy, F1, BLEU) and how they are computed (datasets, averaging procedures, thresholds) to avoid ambiguity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clearly defined error bars
rubrics_metrics.description: "Clearly defined error bars."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reporting variability, explicitly state what error bars represent (e.g., standard deviation, standard error, confidence intervals) and how they were computed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report central tendency and variation
rubrics_metrics.description: "A description of results with central tendency (e.g. mean) & variation (e.g. stddev)."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report means/medians together with measures of spread (stddev, IQR, confidence intervals) across runs, folds, or trials to convey uncertainty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use proper statistical testing and quantify uncertainty
rubrics_metrics.description: The paper emphasizes that "statistical analysis is seldom conducted in ML research" and highlights the need for proper statistical testing rather than inappropriate claims of significance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply appropriate statistical tests, correct for multiple comparisons where required, and avoid claiming significance without proper methodology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid selective reporting and adaptive overfitting
rubrics_metrics.description: "Selective reporting of results and ignoring the danger of adaptive overfitting" are identified as causes of irreproducibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report experimental search procedures, hyperparameter sweeps, failures and negative results where relevant; be transparent about model selection procedures to reduce adaptive bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specify model and training procedure fully (avoid under-specification)
rubrics_metrics.description: The paper lists "Misspecification or under-specification of the model or training procedure" as a frequent cause of irreproducibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide full specification of architectures, loss functions, optimization algorithms, hyperparameter values, initialization, stopping criteria and any non-deterministic behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide access to training data or alternatives when confidential
rubrics_metrics.description: Dataset confidentiality is a common objection to sharing. The paper suggests: provide complementary empirical results on an open-source benchmark dataset in addition to results on confidential data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If original data cannot be shared for privacy or IP reasons, include experiments on public benchmarks and detailed descriptions of the confidential dataset characteristics where permissible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for computation infrastructure limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: The paper notes that experiments may be computationally infeasible to reproduce (very large models) and discusses implications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When experiments are computationally heavy, provide smaller-scale reproductions, detailed resource descriptions, or containerized environments; discuss compute requirements clearly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use containers and standard tooling to encapsulate environments
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation to consider software containers (e.g., Docker) to encapsulate OS components, code and data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide container images or environment specifications (Dockerfiles, requirements.txt, conda env) to reduce environment-related reproducibility issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage independent reimplementation and verification
rubrics_metrics.description: Availability of code is helpful, but reimplementation from the paper is valuable — "There is significant value in reimplementing an algorithm directly from its description in a paper."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write papers with enough detail for independent reimplementation; make reference implementations available to aid verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use checklists to enforce minimal reporting items
rubrics_metrics.description: The ML reproducibility checklist provides minimal reporting items to include in manuscripts; checklists are "meant to provide the minimal information that must be included in a manuscript, and are not necessarily exhaustive."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should complete the checklist (Yes/No/NA plus optional comments) to document inclusion of key reproducibility items; reviewers can use checklist answers to guide assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make reproducibility reports public and archived
rubrics_metrics.description: Reproducibility challenge reports were made publicly available on OpenReview and select reports archived in ReScience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publish reproducibility reports and reimplementation code publicly to provide examples and archival evidence of independent verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report code availability and reviewer engagement with code
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers were asked to indicate whether code was provided and whether they looked at it and found it useful (survey responses tracked: e.g., if provided, did you look at the code? If provided, was the code useful in guiding your review?).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should clearly state code availability on submission; reviewers should record whether they examined code and how it influenced their review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explore experimental sources of variability (hyperparameters, random seeds)
rubrics_metrics.description: The background highlights failures to explore variables that affect conclusions, including hyper-parameter search and different random initializations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct and report hyperparameter searches, sensitivity analyses, multiple random seeds/initializations, and variation across runs to demonstrate robustness of claimed improvements.
